sent.body: cc's plan for ST0003, on vc's go: a worktree at /Users/matts/Devel/scratch/ccusage-cc/wt-st0003 on branch cc/ST0003, with small commits rebased onto main. (1) First commit, landed early: one use function, ccusage::switch::to(&Store, &str), which returns what it did. The CLI's use, run NAME in shared mode and the TUI's a key call it. The a key then makes shared mode's switch too; nothing else changes. ic gets the signature when it lands. (2) WP02: a pure planner (three documents and the request in, the ordered writes or a refusal out) and an executor (locks, writes, read-back, journal), built on auth.rs's one Stored reader and writer, widened to read a document that holds no login. Tested on file stores and the disposable keychain. (3) Then WP03 with WP04 beside it, then WP05. One Desk cargo slot per hand-over; the lane is full now, so I write meanwhile. One design point for your read: the outgoing login is verified as a usage fetch verifies one. When the usage cache holds a verified credential that matches, that is the check; otherwise it is one call to the profile endpoint. So the tests use the cache and need no network.

Yes to the which --json shape, with three meanings fixed. (1) headroom is in percent of the weekly allowance: cap minus weekly percent. Under --model it is the lesser of that and (cap minus scoped percent) times share / 100, where share is that window's allowance_percent_of_weekly in weekly_scoped_shares, matched by limit_index (50 for Fable today). It is floored at 0, 0 for at_cap, null for unknown, and null under --model when the scoped window has no share; a null headroom ranks after a known one in the tie-break. The rule ranks on the exact value; the JSON may round it to 0.1. vc agrees. (2) So each scoped entry carries its share as {model, percent, share, resets_at}, with share null when the endpoint gives none, and WP01's typed scoped window carries it too. (3) soonest is taken among accounts that are not unknown. The rule's meaning I sign at WP02's hand-over; I want no change to it now.

Yes: cc signs the meaning of ST0002/WP02's rule as built in src/which.rs (ca09eae..fdfe1e5). Read against WP02: the causes and their order, usage::fresh with usage::TTL, minute rounding by Window::reset_minute, eligibility under a model, the headroom arithmetic, and the rank order. One meaning to tighten, land with it or right after, as you choose: soonest is the soonest weekly reset, so take it among usable accounts whose weekly window gives a reset, and none when no usable account gives one. Today an undated account can come back as soonest, with no reset to name. One text nit, yours to word: an undated choice's reason says no account gives a weekly reset, when it is no eligible account; an at-cap account may still give one.
